# k0rdent_project (Data Source)

One project, read rather than managed.

Use it to name a project another configuration owns, from the state boundary that holds the clusters and networks inside it. `status` is what to read on that side: a project at `deleting` still answers reads and still holds its name, and a cluster created in one is refused.

Unlike every other data source here it takes no `region` and no `project`. A project lives on the global control-plane tier and is addressed inside an organization. A project's `id` is normally held by one organization, so `organization_id` can be left out and is then looked up. If more than one organization holds the id, the read is refused and `organization_id` has to be set.

A credential scoped to a project can read that project, with or without `organization_id`. The platform refuses such a credential a project's read by id, because it checks that read against the organization, so the provider reads the project from the project list instead, which shows the credential its own projects.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A project another configuration owns, to build in without managing it.

data "k0rdent_project" "platform" {
  id = "platform-shared"

  # Optional. Without it, the organization is looked up, which fails if two
  # organizations use this id.
  organization_id = "org-acme"

  # Fail the plan, not partway through the apply, if the project isn't active.
  lifecycle {
    postcondition {
      condition     = self.status == "active"
      error_message = "platform-shared is ${self.status}, so anything created inside it will be refused."
    }
  }
}

# A provider for that project. Resources use it with `provider = k0rdent.shared`.
provider "k0rdent" {
  alias   = "shared"
  region  = "us-texas-1"
  project = data.k0rdent_project.platform.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Project id. This is the value the provider block's `project` takes. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.

### Optional

- `organization_id` (String) The organization the project is in. Looked up from `id` when left out, in the one list request that reads the project. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the project was created, as RFC 3339. The resource does not carry this and does not need to: it is read every run here and compared against nothing.
- `description` (String) Free-form text describing it, for people to read.
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name, if the project has one.
- `region` (String) The region the project is locked to. Every regional resource in the project has to be in it, so it's the value their `region`, or the provider's, takes. Null for a project made before regions were required.
- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this project.
- `status` (String) Lifecycle status. `active` is usable. `suspended` and `disabled` are steady states the platform can hold a project in. `deleting` means a teardown has been accepted and the project takes no new work, so a configuration that is about to build inside it should check for it rather than discover it as a 409 part way through an apply.
